newsitem.title: USA: No criminal charges against Maine egg farm.
newsitem.headline: No criminal charges against Maine egg farm.

text.p: Federal prosecutors have declined to file criminal charges against managers of a Maine egg farm that faces $3.6 million in fines for alleged safety violations, officials said Tuesday.

U.S. Labor Secretary Robert Reich had asked the Justice Department to consider criminal prosecution of managers of DeCoster Egg Farms for exposing the largely Hispanic migrant workforce to what Reich "sweatshop-like" conditions.

Maine's U.S. Attorney Jay McCloskey said he decided not to file criminal charges, in part, because pursuing the case might delay the Labor Department's efforts to take civil action against the company.

The fines proposed by the Labor Department earlier this year are a "much greater" punishment than could be obtained through criminal prosecution, said McCloskey, whose office had investigated if DeCoster officials lied to government safety investigators.

DeCoster - the largest producer of brown eggs in the United States - has disputed Reich's accusations but acknowledged there were problems in working and employee housing conditions that it says are being corrected.

The controversy has prompted four New England supermarket chains to boycott DeCoster's eggs, but company officials say the privately owned company has partially offset that sales loss by increasing exports to Asia.
